aboutAuthor: Walter Isaacson connects Leonardo's art to his science, showing how his curiosity across disciplines—anatomy, optics, hydraulics, theater—fueled creative genius. Based on 7,200 pages of notebooks.

points.heading: Currency in Italy in 1500
points.body: CURRENCY IN ITALY IN 1500 The ducat was the gold coin of Venice. The florin was the gold coin of Florence. Both contained 3.5 grams (0.12 ounces) of gold, which would make them worth about $138 in 2017. One ducat or florin was worth approximately 7 lire or 120 soldi, which were silver coins. NOTE RE...
